sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Manish Mathur,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in an Fir bearing
Case Crime No. 117 of 2023, under Sections 406, 420, 418, 504, 506 Ipc, Police Station Kotwali
Bhinga, District Shrawasti.

3.  As per contents of FIR, allegation levelled is that the applicant and co-accused are co-proprietors of Raftar Infratec Traders and had obtained a loan from the informant for the purpose of expansion of business but the said loan was not returned.

It is submitted that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the charges levelled against him and that ex-facie the allegations levelled are purely commercial in nature which are unnecessarily being given a criminal colour.
It is submitted that previous criminal history of one case has been explained.
5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed anticipatory bail application but does not dispute the said facts.

6. Upon consideration of submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perusal of material on record, it appears that entire gist of allegation levelled against the applicant is of not returning a loan amount which was advanced as business transaction by the informant.
The aspect of cheating as opposed to breach of promise would require consideration.
The applicant's previous criminal has already been explained.
Charge sheet has already been filed in the matter.
The applicant has undertaken to cooperate during the course of trial.

Thus, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal and others versus State (NCT of Delhi) and another (2020)5 SCC 1, it would be appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to applicant under Section 438 Cr.P.C./482 BNSS.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is made clear that the observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

9. The application stands disposed of.
